In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

We begin this session with the exegesis of Surat al-Ghashiyah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿Has there come to you the news of the Overwhelming (Ghashiyah)?﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 1]. The basmalah is a verse of the Book of Allah in its own right, not part of the surah before it or the surah after it; rather it is an independent verse. For this reason, the preponderant opinion is that it is not part of al-Fatihah, and that the beginning of al-Fatihah is ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, and so on.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Has there come to you the news of the Overwhelming (Ghashiyah)?﴾ The address is either to the Prophet (ﷺ), or to everyone who is capable of being addressed. This occurs frequently in the Qur'an: Allah directs the address either to the Prophet (ﷺ) or to everyone who is able to be addressed and is fit to be addressed. However, at times it is specifically directed to the Messenger (peace be upon him), such as ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [al-Sharh 1]; this can only be addressed to the Messenger (peace be upon him). ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ [al-Ma'idah 67]; this can only be addressed to the Messenger (ﷺ).

At other times the generality is preferred, such as ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ [al-Talaq 1]. Its beginning is addressed to the Prophet (peace be upon him), while its latter part, ﴿when you divorce﴾, is general.

So His saying ﴿Has there come to you the news of the Overwhelming?﴾ may be an address directed to the Messenger (ﷺ) alone, with his ummah following him, or it may be general to everyone who is capable of being addressed.

The interrogative here is for arousing interest, like His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ [al-Saff 10]. It may also be for magnifying the matter, due to the greatness of this news about the Overwhelming.

﴿The news of the Overwhelming (hadith al-ghashiyah)﴾ means its account. Al-Ghashiyah is the great calamity that envelops people, and it is the Day of Resurrection, about which Allah spoke frequently in the Qur'an, describing it with great attributes, such as His saying: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. The Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she was nursing, and every pregnant one will drop her load, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they will not be intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe﴾ [al-Hajj 1-2].

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, divided people on that day into two categories, saying: ﴿Faces on that Day will be humbled (2), toiling and weary﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 2, 3]. ﴿Humbled﴾ means: abased, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And you will see them exposed to it, humbled by abasement, looking with a furtive glance﴾ [ash-Shura 45]. So the meaning of ﴿humbled﴾ is abased.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 88, verse 3:

﴿Laboring, exhausted﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 3] "Laboring" means doing work that results in nasb (fatigue), which is weariness.

The scholars said: This is because on the Day of Resurrection they will be burdened with dragging chains and shackles and wading through the Fire of Hell, may Allah protect us, just as a man wades through mud. So they are laboring and weary from the work they are assigned on the Day of Resurrection, because it is work of punishment and retribution, may Allah grant us well-being. It is not as some people have said, that what is meant by them are the disbelievers whose effort went astray in the life of this world while they thought they were doing good in their works. That is because Allah restricted this with His words: ﴿Faces that Day﴾, meaning on the day when the Overwhelming Event comes, and this can only be the Day of Resurrection. So they are ﴿laboring, exhausted﴾ by what they are assigned of dragging chains and shackles and wading through the Fire of Hell, may Allah protect us and you from it.

**Verse 4: "They will burn in a scorching fire."** [Al-Ghashiyah: 4]

Meaning: they will be made to enter the Fire of Hell—may Allah protect us from it—the scorching fire, whose heat has reached such a degree that it has been given a superiority over the fire of this world by sixty-nine parts. That is, the entire fire of this world, with all of the most intense heat it can have, the fire of Hell is sixty-nine times more intense than it.

What shows you the intensity of its heat is that this sun's heat reaches us despite the great distance between us and it, and although it passes through atmospheres that are extremely cold, this heat that you feel reaches us, especially in the summer days. So the Fire—may Allah protect us and you from it—is a scorching fire.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 88, verse 5:

﴿They will be given drink from a boiling spring﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 88:5], ﴿They will have no food except from thorny plants﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 88:6]. When He had explained their place, and that they are in the blazing Fire of Hell (may Allah protect us), He explained their food and drink, saying: ﴿They will be given drink﴾, meaning these faces, ﴿from a boiling spring﴾, meaning one of extreme heat. This concerns their drink. Yet this drink does not come to them with ease, nor are they given to drink whenever they are thirsty. No, they are brought it only when their thirst becomes severe (may Allah protect us) and they call for help, as the Most High said: ﴿And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces. Wretched is the drink﴾ [al-Kahf 18:29]. When this water comes near their faces, it scorches them and their flesh falls away; and when it enters their bellies, the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And they will be given boiling water, which cuts their intestines to pieces﴾ [Muhammad 47:15]. Thus they gain nothing from it, neither outwardly nor inwardly: not outwardly, by its coolness cooling their faces, and not inwardly, by quenching their thirst. Rather, they are relieved (may Allah protect us) with this water. Therefore He said: ﴿They will be given drink from a boiling spring﴾.

If someone says: How can this spring be in the Fire of Hell, when the normal custom is that water extinguishes fire? Is that not so?

The answer: The affairs of the Hereafter are not measured by the affairs of this world. If they were measured by the affairs of this world, we could not imagine how it would be. Is it not the case that the sun will draw near to people's heads on the Day of Resurrection to the distance of a mil! The mil is either the mil of the kohl-stick, which is half a finger's length, or the mil of distance, a kilometre and a third or thereabouts. Even if this were so, were the Hereafter like this world, it would have roasted people to a crisp. But the Hereafter is not measured by this world.

Also, on the Day of Resurrection people will be gathered in one place: some of them will be in intense darkness, and some of them in light: ﴿Their light will run before them and on their right hand﴾ [al-Tahrim 66:8]. They will be gathered in one place and will sweat: some of them will have sweat reaching their ankles, some will have it reaching their knees, and some will have it reaching their waists, yet they are all in one place. Thus the conditions of the Hereafter may not be measured by the conditions of this world.

So if someone says: How can there be water in the Fire?

We say: Firstly, the conditions of the Hereafter are not measured by the conditions of this world.

Secondly, Allah is over all things capable. Behold, we now find that fire is kindled from green trees, as the Most High said: ﴿He who made for you fire from the green tree, and behold, from it you kindle﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:80]. The green tree is moist, yet when some of it is struck against another, or struck with a flint, fire springs forth from it: a hot, dry fire, though the wood is moist and cool. Allah is over all things capable. So they are given drink from a boiling spring in the Fire, and this does not contradict the power of the Most High.

As for their food, He says: ﴿They will have no food except from thorny plants (ḍarīʿ), which neither nourish nor satisfy hunger﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 6–7].

(Ḍarīʿ) They said: it is a plant with large thorns; when it dries it is not grazed by animals, nor by livestock, but if it is green the camels graze on it. It is called shibraq among us. This ḍarīʿ is a thorny plant: when it dries it is not grazed, because it is thorns, and when it is green the camels graze on it. They—may Allah protect us—are in the Fire of Hell, having no food except this ḍarīʿ. But do not think that the ḍarīʿ in the Fire of Hell is like the ḍarīʿ of this world; it differs from it greatly. For this reason He says: ﴿which neither nourishes﴾, so it does not benefit the bodies outwardly, ﴿nor satisfies hunger﴾, so it does not benefit them inwardly. There is no good in it at all; it contains only thorns, a great choking, bitterness, and a foul stench from which they gain nothing.

As for their food, He says: ﴿They will have no food except from thorny plants (ḍarīʿ), which neither nourish nor satisfy hunger﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 6–7].

(Ḍarīʿ) They said: it is a plant with large thorns; when it dries it is not grazed by animals, nor by livestock, but if it is green the camels graze on it. It is called shibraq among us. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned the second category of people on the Day of the Overwhelming, saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be full of delight﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 8] and so on to the end of the verse. We will mention it, if Allah wills, in the next session.

We ask Allah the Exalted to protect us and you from the Fire, to grant us and you the Abode of Permanence, for He is over all things capable.

* * *

(...) To proceed: this is the meeting of the Open Door, the sixtieth meeting since its beginning, and it is the second meeting of the month of Muharram in the year one thousand four hundred and fifteen, and it is the seventh day of the month.

In this meeting we speak about the words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Faces that Day will be full of delight (8). Pleased with their striving (9). In a lofty Garden (10). Wherein they will hear no ill speech﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 8-11], and so on to the end of the verses.

Allah, Glorified and Exalted, divided people on the Day of Resurrection into two categories:

The first category: faces that Day will be humbled, toiling and weary, and this has already been discussed.

The second category: faces that are delighted (nā'imah), meaning delighted by what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has bestowed upon them of joy and abundant reward, because they knew of that while they were in their graves. Indeed, a person in his grave is made to enjoy comfort: a door to Paradise is opened for him, so that its breeze and bliss reach him, and thus they are delighted.

Concerning His words ﴿Pleased with their striving﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 9], that is: pleased with their deeds which they performed in the world, because through them they have reached this bliss, this joy and this delight. So they are pleased with their striving, in contrast to the first faces, which are angry—we seek refuge in Allah—and not pleased with what they had put forward.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 88, verse 10:

﴿In a lofty Garden﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 10]. The Garden (al-Jannah) is the abode of bliss that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prepared for His friends on the Day of Resurrection. In it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [as-Sajdah: 17]. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Certainly will the believers have succeeded. They who are during their prayer humbly submissive. And they who turn away from ill speech. And they who are paying zakah, doing [it]﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Those are the inheritors who will inherit al-Firdaws; they will abide therein eternally﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 1-11]. And Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And therein is whatever the souls desire and that which the eyes find delight in, and you therein will abide eternally﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 71]. So they are in a lofty Garden. Al-'uluw (highness) is the opposite of al-suful (lowness), so it is above the seven heavens. It is well known that on the Day of Resurrection the seven heavens and the earths will pass away, and nothing will remain except the Garden and the Fire. So it is lofty, and the highest and central part of it is al-Firdaws, above which is the Throne of the Lord, Majestic and Exalted.

ﷻ﴿There you will not hear any vain talk﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 11]. That is, in this Paradise you will not hear any vain speech or any frivolous soul; rather, everything in it is serious, everything in it is peace, everything in it is glorification (tasbih), praise (tahmid), declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and magnification (takbir). They are inspired to glorify God just as they are inspired to breathe; that is, it is not burdensome to them, nor do they become tired of it. They are always in the remembrance of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, in glorification, in companionship and in joy, coming to one another and visiting one another, in a delight without equal. We ask Allah to make us and you among its people.

﴿Therein is a flowing spring﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 88:12]. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made clear that this spring consists of rivers. ﴿Therein are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste never changes, and rivers of wine, delicious to those who drink, and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad 47:15].

﴿Flowing﴾ means that it flows wherever its people wish. It needs no digging of a channel and no construction of a trench. As Ibn al-Qayyim (may God have mercy on him) said:

Its rivers flow without any trench,
Glory be to the One who holds them back from overflowing.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 88, verses 13–16:

﴿In it are couches raised high (13), and cups set in place (14), and cushions lined up (15), and carpets spread out (16)﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 13–16], note the contrast:

﴿In it are couches raised high﴾ lofty, on which they recline, enjoying fruits; ﴿they and their spouses, in shade, reclining on couches﴾ [Ya-Sin: 56].

﴿And cups set in place﴾. Al-akwab is the plural of kub (kub), which is a drinking vessel or the like. ﴿Set in place﴾ means: not removed from them; rather they are placed for them, so that whenever they wish they may drink from them, from these four rivers mentioned earlier.

﴿And cushions lined up (15) and carpets spread out﴾. Al-namariq is the plural of numruqah (numruqah), which is a pillow or that which one leans upon, lined up in the finest manner, so that the eye delights in them before the body delights in reclining upon them.

﴿And carpets spread out﴾. Al-zarabi is the highest kind of furnishings. ﴿Spread out﴾ means laid out everywhere. And do not suppose that these cushions, these cups, these couches and these carpets resemble what is in this world; for if they resembled what is in this world, we would know the bliss of the Hereafter and know its reality. But they do not resemble it, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [as-Sajdah: 17]. The names are one, but the realities differ. For this reason Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "There is nothing in the Hereafter of what is in this world except the names alone"[[Narrated by Hannad in az-Zuhd (3), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th wa'n-Nushur (332).]]. So we do not know the reality of these blessings mentioned in Paradise, although we witness things in this world that match them in name; yet there is a difference between this and that.

* * *

(...) The final outcome belongs to the God-fearing, and there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers. I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, the seal of the prophets and leader of the God-fearing. May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the sixty-first session of the sittings known as "The Open Door Meeting," which are held every Thursday of each week. This is the fourteenth day of the month of Muharram in the year 1415 AH. We begin, as usual, with whatever is feasible of the tafsir (exegesis) of the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. In the previous lesson we reached the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Do they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah 17].

When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, established in this surah the account of al-Ghashiyah (the Overwhelming Event), which is the Day of Resurrection, and explained that people divide into two categories: faces that are humbled, labouring and weary, that will burn in a scorching fire, and faces that are pleasant, pleased with their striving, and explained the recompense of each of these, He said: ﴿Do they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾. This interrogation is one of reproach; that is, Allah reproaches those who denied what Allah had reported about the Day of Resurrection and about reward and punishment. He rebuked them for their turning away from contemplating the signs of Allah, the Exalted, that lie before them. He began with the camels because the most common thing people dealt with at that time was camels: they ride them, milk them, eat their meat, and benefit from their wool, along with other benefits. So He said: ﴿Do they not look at the camels﴾, and they are the mature camels (al-abā'ir).

﴿how they were created﴾ means: how Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created them with this large, load-bearing body. You find the camel walking long distances which a person can reach only with great difficulty, and it bears this while carrying. You also find the camel carrying loads while it is kneeling, then it stands up with its load without needing any help. Ordinarily an animal can hardly stand when loaded while kneeling, but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gave these camels strength and capability for the benefit of humans; for a person could not load them while they are standing because of their height, but Allah, the Exalted, made it easy for him to load them while they kneel, and then they rise with their burden. As Allah, the Exalted, said in Surah Ya-Sin: ﴿And for them therein are benefits and drinks; will they not then be grateful?﴾ [Ya-Sin 73]. Their benefits are numerous and cannot be counted, and their owners who work with them know about this better than we do. Therefore He said: ﴿Do they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾, and He did not mention other animals such as sheep, cattle and gazelles, or others, because, as I told you, the camel is the most generally beneficial of animals and the most advantageous for people.

And at the sky, how it was raised [Q 88:18]. That is: and they look at the sky, how it was raised, with what is in it of stars, the sun, the moon, and other great signs, many of which have not been clarified until now. We do not say that these heavenly signs are all the signs; rather, there may be great and mighty signs that we do not yet comprehend.

As for His saying, "how it was raised" (kayfa rufiʿat), it means: raised to this great height. And despite this, it has no pillars, although it is the custom that ceilings are only supported by pillars. But this great, protected ceiling stands without pillars: "Allah is the One who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see" [Q 13:2].

And to the mountains, how they were set up. [Al-Ghashiyah 88:19]

These are the great mountains that carry rocks and separate, adjoining pieces of differing kinds. The mountains are composed of many stones and many types, including various minerals, and they are adjacent to one another. Yet you find, for example, that this vein within the rock contains minerals that are not found in the rock close to it. Those who specialize in geology (al-jiyulujiya) know how God set up these great mountains. Glorified and exalted is He, He set them at this height so that they would be firm bulwarks (rawasi) on the earth, lest it shake with the people. Had God, Mighty and Majestic, not created these mountains, the earth would have shaken with its inhabitants, because the earth is in the midst of water, with water surrounding it on every side. And what do you think of a sphere that is placed in the midst of water? It would move, convulse, roll about at times and overturn at others. But God made these mountains firm bulwarks that hold the earth steady, just as tent pegs (al-atnab) hold up a tent. They are fixed and steadfast against the great storms that occur on the earth and that demolish the buildings erected by human beings, yet these mountains do not budge; they remain firmly set even when great storms come. Indeed, among their benefits is that they shield from the mighty, violent winds that blow forth from the seas or from elsewhere, lest they sweep away the people. This is something observed: you find those who live on the slopes of mountains and beneath them in the earth are in safety from the great windstorms that come from behind the mountain. So they have great benefits, and they are firm bulwarks. Even if all of creation gathered to place a range of mountains like this chain, they could not do so, however far their craft, strength and power advanced and however long their span of time. They would not be able to bring forth mountains like these.

Some scholars have said: these mountains are fixed in the earth to the same extent as their height in the sky. That is, for example, a mountain has a root and a base deep within the earth at a depth equal to its height above. This is not far-fetched: God may have established the mountain in the earth to the extent of what it is in the sky, so that the winds do not shake it. For this reason the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains lest it shake with you, and rivers and roads, that you may be guided. And landmarks; and by the star they are guided﴾ [An-Nahl 16:15-16].

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And at the mountains, how they are raised? (19) And at the earth, how it is spread out?﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 19-20]. How Allah spread out this vast earth and made it a wide, level surface so that people can live upon it by farming, building and other things. Now consider: if the earth were a slope, not spread out, meaning like the mountains that one must climb and ascend, it would be difficult, and people would not be able to settle on it. But Allah the Mighty and Majestic made it a level surface, smoothed out for creation.

Some scholars have used this verse as evidence that the earth is not spherical but a extended flat surface. However, this inference is open to question, because there are verses which indicate that the earth is spherical, and reality bears witness to this. Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾ [az-Zumar 5]. Al-takwir means al-tadwir (turning around something in a circle). It is well known that night and day succeed one another over the earth; if they are wrapped around one another, then the earth must be round. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿When the sky is split open (1), and it listens to its Lord and is obliged to (2). And when the earth is stretched out (3), and it casts out what is in it and empties itself﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 1-4]. He said: ﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾. It has come in a hadith that on the Day of Resurrection it will be stretched out like a leather hide (adim), meaning stretched like skin, until there are no mountains, no valleys, no trees and no buildings in it; the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, will leave it as a smooth level plain, in which you will see no crookedness or elevation.[[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir (3549), from the hadith of ʿAli ibn al-Husayn.]] So His saying: ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ — when will the sky be split open? We all know that it will not be split open except on the Day of Resurrection, and that it is not split open now. Therefore His saying: ﴿And when the earth is stretched out (3) and casts out what is in it and empties itself﴾ refers to the Day of Resurrection. So it is not stretched out now. Then what is it? It is round.

The observable and certain reality now is that it is undoubtedly spherical. The proof of this is that if you travelled in a straight line from here, from the Kingdom, heading west, you would arrive from the direction of the east, and you would not find anything (...), you would circle the earth and come back to the point from which you set out. Likewise in reverse: if you travelled heading east, you would find yourself returning to the point from which you stood, from the direction of the west. So it is now a matter beyond doubt that it is spherical.

If someone says: if it is as you claim, spherical, how do the waters of the seas remain upon it if it is round?

We say in answer to this: He who holds the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission holds the seas from overflowing upon people and drowning them, and Allah is capable of all things.

Some people of knowledge said: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [at-Takwir 6], meaning they are confined and prevented from overflowing upon people, like a thing that is tied up (yusjar; tied).

In any case, divine power is not something we can contest. We say: the power of Allah the Mighty and Majestic has held these seas from overflowing upon the people of the earth and drowning them, even though the earth is round.

Then the Exalted said, after He had mentioned these four signs—the camels, the sky, the mountains, and the earth—addressing His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿So remind, [for] you are only a reminder﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 21]. Allah commanded him to remind, and He did not single out anyone for the reminding; that is, He did not say: "Remind so-and-so and so-and-so." So the reminding is general, because the Messenger ﷺ was sent to all of mankind. Remind every person, in every state and in every place. The Prophet ﷺ reminded, and his successors after him, who took his place in his community in knowledge, action and calling to Allah, also reminded. But does every person benefit from this reminder?

The answer: No. ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 55]. As for the one who is not a believer, the reminder establishes the proof against him but does not benefit him. Only the believer benefits from the reminder. We say: if you see that your heart does not take heed through the reminder, then suspect it of what? Of lacking faith, because Allah says: ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers﴾. So when you are reminded and do not find in your heart any impression or benefit, then blame yourself and know that there is a deficiency in your faith, for if your faith were complete you would have benefited from the reminder. It must be that the reminder benefits the believer.

﴿You are only a reminder﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 21] means that Muhammad ﷺ is nothing but a reminder and a conveyor. As for guidance, in whose hand is it? In the hand of Allah: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 272]. The Prophet ﷺ performed the reminding and the admonishing until his last breath in life. Indeed, at the end of his life he said: "The prayer, the prayer, and what your right hands possess"[[Narrated by Ibn Majah (1625) from the hadith of Umm Salamah.]], until he was gasping with it ﷺ. He, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, reminded from the time he was sent and was told: ﴿Arise and warn﴾ [al-Muddaththir 2], until Allah took him. He spared no effort in reminding in every place and at every time, despite the harm he suffered from his own people and from others. Whoever among you has read history, the Prophetic biography (al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah), knows what befell him from the people of Makkah, from his own people who were the closest of people to him, who knew him and called him "al-Amin" (the Trustworthy), naming him so and trusting him. They even made him the arbiter in placing the Black Stone in the Kaabah. When they demolished the Kaabah and reached the place of the Stone, they said: "Who will set the Stone?" They disputed among themselves, each tribe saying: "We are the ones who should take charge of placing the Stone in its place." Then the Prophet ﷺ came and they made him the arbiter between them, and he ordered that a cloak be spread out and that each of these tribes hold a corner of this cloak until they raised it. When they reached its place, he took it with his noble hand and set it in its place[[Narrated by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi (115), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan (9208) and al-Dala'il (415), from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib.]]. They used to call him "al-Amin," but when Allah honored him with prophethood, the standards were reversed, and they began to say: "He is a sorcerer, a soothsayer, a poet, a madman, and a liar," and they hurled every insult at him. So the Messenger ﷺ reminds, and his duty is only reminding.

From here we derive that we are not obligated to guide people, and we can never guide people, not even those closest to us: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Qasas 56]. So we should not despair when we remind a person and find him obstinate, disputing, or saying: "Leave me alone," or "I will do what I want," or the like. Allah said to His Prophet: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers﴾ [ash-Shu'ara 3]. Do not destroy yourself if they do not believe; their faith is for their own benefit and their disbelief is not your concern. Therefore He said: ﴿You are not over them a controller﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 22], meaning you have no authority over them and no control over them. To whom belong authority and control? To Allah, Lord of the worlds. Your duty is to convey; you are to convey. Is it your duty that people act upon it? No. That is up to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and authority and control belong to Allah.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 88, verses 23–24:

﴿Except one who turns away and disbelieves (23). Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment (24).﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 23, 24] The scholars said: "Illa" (except) here means "lakin" (but). That is, the exception in the verse is disjunctive (munqati') and not connected (muttasil). The difference between the connected and the disjunctive exception is that in the connected one, the excepted item is of the same kind as that from which it is excepted, whereas in the disjunctive one, it is foreign to it. For example, if we said that it is connected, the meaning of the verse would be: "You are not over them a controller, except one who turns away and disbelieves, so you are over them a controller." This is not the case. Rather, the meaning is: "But whoever turns away and disbelieves, after you have reminded him, Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment." So whoever turns away and disbelieves after the revelation revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has reached him, he will be punished; ﴿except one who turns away and disbelieves﴾.

Tawalli (turning away) means aversion: he does not turn toward the truth, does not accept the truth, and does not listen to the truth. Even if he hears it with his ear, he does not hear it with his heart, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger and do not turn away from him while you are hearing (20). And do not be like those who say, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾ [al-Anfal: 20, 21], meaning: they do not submit.

So here the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿except one who turns away and disbelieves﴾. ﴿Turned away﴾ means he turned aside, and ﴿disbelieved﴾ means he was arrogant and did not accept what the Messenger (peace be upon him) brought.

﴿Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. Allah said: ﴿And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment short of the greater punishment﴾ [as-Sajdah: 21]. The greatest punishment is on the Day of Resurrection. Here He said ﴿the greatest﴾ without mentioning the thing it is compared to; that is, He did not say "the greatest of such-and-such." So he has reached the utmost in greatness, hardship and humiliation, and we seek refuge in Allah. Everyone who turns away and disbelieves, Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment.

Is there a lesser punishment?

We say: Yes, there is a lesser punishment in this world. The one who turns away and opposes may be afflicted with illnesses in his body, his mind, his family, his wealth, and his society, and all of this, compared with the punishment of the Fire, is a lesser punishment. But the greatest punishment is only on the Day of Resurrection, and for this reason He said after it:

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 88, verses 25–26:

﴿Indeed, to Us is their return (25). Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning.﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 25, 26].

﴿To Us is their return﴾ means: their place of return. So the return is to Allah. No matter how far a person flees, he is returning to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, even if his life is prolonged; he is returning to Allah. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿O mankind, indeed you are toiling toward your Lord with arduous toil, and you will meet Him﴾ [Al-Inshiqaq: 6]. Prepare yourself, my brother, for this meeting, for you will surely meet your Lord. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is none among you but that his Lord will speak to him, with no interpreter between them," directly, without a translator; Allah will speak to him on the Day of Resurrection. "Then he will look to his right and see nothing but what he has sent forward, and he will look to his left (meaning on the left) and see nothing but what he has sent forward, and he will look in front of his face and see nothing but the Fire before his face. So protect yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (6539) from the hadith of 'Adi ibn Hatim.]]. Every one of us will be alone with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection, who will make him acknowledge his sins; He will say: "You did such-and-such on such-and-such a day," until he admits and confesses. When he admits and confesses, Allah the Exalted says: "I concealed it for you in the world, and I forgive it for you today"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2441) and Muslim (2786/52), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.]]. How many sins has Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, concealed! How many sins have we committed that no one knew of, yet Allah the Exalted knew of them. Our stance regarding these sins is to seek forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to increase righteous deeds that expiate evil deeds, until we meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, while we are upon that which pleases Him, glorified and exalted is He.

﴿Indeed, to Us is their return (25). Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning.﴾ We will reckon with them. The scholars said: the manner of the reckoning is not a scrutinizing examination, for a person who is scrutinized would be destroyed. If Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, were to scrutinize you (...) in the reckoning, you would be destroyed.

Suppose He scrutinized you regarding one of the blessings, such as sight. You cannot find anything you do that could match the blessing of sight. The blessing of breath: the breath that goes out and comes in without any hardship and without any effort. A person speaks, sleeps, eats and drinks, yet he does not feel the breath nor know its worth until he is afflicted with something that obstructs his breath; then he remembers the blessing of Allah. But as long as he is in good health, it is a normal thing. However, if he were afflicted with suffocation, he would know the value of the blessing. So if he were scrutinized, he would be destroyed; as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said to 'Aishah: "Whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning will be destroyed," or he said: "will be punished"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6536) and Muslim (2876/79), from the hadith of 'Aishah.]].

However, as for the manner of the reckoning: as for the believer, Allah the Exalted will be alone with him, with no one else present, and will make him acknowledge his sins: "You did such-and-such, you did such-and-such, you did such-and-such," until when he admits them, Allah the Exalted says: "I concealed it for you in the world, and I forgive it for you today."

As for the disbelievers, they are not reckoned in this manner, because they have no good deeds to erase their evil deeds. Rather, their deeds are counted against them, they are made to acknowledge them before the whole world, and they are disgraced by them, and it is proclaimed before the witnesses: ﴿These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Surely the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud: 18][[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2441) and Muslim (2786/52), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.]]. We seek refuge with Allah from abandonment.

With this, the discussion of this great surah concludes. It is one of the two surahs which the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite at the great gatherings. He would recite in the two 'Eid prayers (Sabbih isma rabbika al-a'la) and (Hal ataka hadith al-ghashiyah), and likewise in the Friday prayer. And at times in the two 'Eids he would recite (Qaf, wal-Quran al-majid) and (Iqtarabat al-sa'ah wa-inshaqqa al-qamar), and in the Friday prayer Surah al-Jumu'ah and al-Munafiqun, varying sometimes one and sometimes the other.

We ask Allah, glorified and exalted is He, to make us and you among those whose faces will be radiant, pleased with their striving, and to take us under His care in this world and the Hereafter; indeed He is capable of all things.
